meta.title: The hammer is the payment
meta.description: Live auctions for graded trading cards on Solana: bid in live rooms, pay in one USDC transaction, sell your own card. Live in beta.

tagline: The live auction room for graded trading cards.

how.heading: Six steps, three roles.
how.intro: Whether you buy, sell or host a room, this is the whole path. Everything happens in your own wallet.

steps.title: Connect your wallet
steps.body: Open Hammerprice in a browser with a Solana wallet, sign in with a free signature and hold some USDC in it.

steps.title: Pick a card and set the terms
steps.body: In Sell, choose a graded card from your wallet and set the price, an optional minimum price and the lot length.

steps.title: Run your room
steps.body: Your room is live as soon as you start it. You can pause and resume it, and you moderate its chat.

steps.title: Place a bid
steps.body: Open a room, choose the next bid or a quick raise and confirm with one signature.

steps.title: The hammer pays
steps.body: When the clock ends, the highest bid wins if it reaches the minimum price. The winner then confirms one payment in their wallet.

steps.title: Check it yourself
steps.body: Public audit pages and proof pages let you recompute a sale or a draw in your browser, so you do not have to trust us.

features.heading: What Hammerprice does.
features.intro: One place for every function, in plain words.

items.title: Rooms and live bidding
items.body: A live room sells its lots one after another on a server clock, so your device's clock does not matter, and a bid is a signed message that the server checks against your USDC. The house runs tutorial rooms and sellers create the real ones, in two sections on the rooms page. A seller can add optional live video; nothing loads until you press Load live video.

items.title: One-transaction settlement
items.body: The winner approves one payment: USDC to the seller, the fee and the card to the winner, all or nothing, as one atomic Solana transaction that costs a fraction of a cent, with no bridge and no custom program.

items.title: Timed auctions
items.body: A card can stay open from one hour to seven days and closes by itself at its deadline, and the winner gets a longer window to pay.

items.title: Selling wizard with AI draft
items.body: The sell wizard drafts a title and a German and an English text with AI for you to review before you go live.

items.title: Pre-moderated chat
items.body: A message waits for approval: the room owner gets a popup with a preview and approves, rejects, mutes or blocks. Links and contact details are refused, the public list shows a bidder number, never a wallet, and visitors can report a message.

items.title: An AI agent that never bids
items.body: On the AI page an agent finds open lots, prepares a bid and drafts a listing; in a room an assistant answers from a fixed FAQ. Everything is labelled AI, a signed-in wallet is required and you confirm every step yourself.

items.title: Telegram bot with alerts
items.body: @hammerpricebot tells you when you are outbid, when you win and when a payment is due. Connect it in your profile with Connect Telegram; it is opt-in, needs no phone number and never bids for you.

items.title: /watch and pre-filled bid links
items.body: Send /watch to the bot (for example /watch 5 or /watch all) and get one short message when each of the next lots of a room opens. Its button opens the room with the bid filled in, and you confirm and sign in your own wallet.

items.title: Packs with published odds
items.body: A pack is a draw from a public pool of cards. The odds, the pool and a commitment hash are public before the first sale.

items.title: Profile and wallet
items.body: A username and a picture, your bids, wins and sales, your notification settings, and the USDC and SOL balance and the cards of your connected wallet. A balance the network does not answer shows as not available, never as a guess.

items.title: Verified randomness (ECVRF)
items.body: Lot orders and pack draws come with a public random proof (ECVRF) that anyone can recompute.

items.title: Public audit pages
items.body: Every paid lot has a public audit page at /verify/ followed by the lot id, linked from the win dialog and the settlement review.

items.title: German and English
items.body: The whole site, the Telegram bot and the assistant's answers are available in German and English, with one switch in the header.

items.title: Wallet support
items.body: Phantom, Solflare and Backpack are supported.

verify.heading: Randomness you can check.
verify.what: Where Hammerprice needs a random result, such as the order of the lots in a show or the card drawn from a pack, it does not pick the result itself. It commits to the input on the Solana chain, waits for a block it cannot know in advance and draws with a verifiable random function (ECVRF, RFC 9381). The result comes with a cryptographic proof, so nobody, including us, can steer it, and anyone can recompute it.
steps: Open a proof page: press See the proof in a room, or use the live example on this page.
Press Recompute it yourself. Your browser rebuilds the input, checks the proof against the published public key and derives the result.
Compare: the lot order or the pack card the page derives must equal the one shown in the room. The commit and reveal transactions link to the Solana explorer.

live.heading: See it live
live.body: The house room's lot order is drawn with this proof. Open the latest one.

also: Every drawn pack has its own proof page at /verify/packs/ followed by the draw id.

blocks.title: The problem
blocks.body: More than 150,000 graded cards already sit as NFTs on Solana, tokenised by the Collector Crypt vault, and there is no live market for them. In a traditional card auction the hammer only starts the paperwork: a payout queue, a chargeback window, a shipping label. The seller is owed the money at the moment of the sale and waits days for it.

blocks.title: The solution
blocks.body: Hammerprice makes the sale and the payout one step for vaulted cards.
